title: Samyama
description: Explore the most advanced stage of mental mastery—the perfect integration of concentration, meditation, and total absorption.

sections.theme: Fix the mind on one point.

sutra.meaning: Fixing the consciousness on one point or region is Dharana.

sections.insight: The yogi must be so familiar with the realm of his mind and emotions, that he should begin to recognize where the thoughts, ideas, images and memories are arising. . Then he can practice the sixth stage of yoga, which is putting his attention to a single object or region.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Is my mind quiet enough to permit me to focus on a single object for a significant duration of my meditation.
sections.practice: Practice focusing on a part of your body, say the heart with eyes closed.
sections.gurudevInsight: You are the light but you do not know because there is a thick curtain around you, an iron curtain around you & this thins down the iron curtain & makes it more transparent that you are able to see that you are light. Another benefit dharanasachayogyatamanasa your mind gets this ability to stay at any one point in the body, to stay at any one point in the body, to stay on any one thing, it is against the ability to intend. Till now there was no intention, you were just like a crowd moving, there was no you inside, you had no intention at all. You are able to have an intention, a direction. [PDF p.92]

sections.theme: A steady, unbroken flow of attention.

sutra.meaning: Dhyana or Meditation is a steady, continuous flow of attention towards one point or region

sections.gurudevInsight: The husk is gone, the sprout moves though it & comes up. They are (1) Yama (2) Niyama (3) Aasana (4) Pranayama (5) Pratyahara (6) Dhyana (7) Dharana (8) Samadhi. He goes into the details of each & what is the result that you can expect from each one of them. Yoga has 8 limbs, like a chair has got four legs, yoga has 8 limbs, or legs. So you just pull 80 one, everything else will come down. If you pull one leg of the chair whole chair comes. [PDF p.80]

sections.theme: The meditator merges with the object.

sutra.meaning: Samadhi is the meditator merging with the object of meditation and losing his self awareness.

sections.insight: When the lines become blurred gradually you become one with awareness.
sections.gurudevInsight: 5) Pratyahara: - swavishyasamprayogechittaswarupalukaarivendriyanaam pratyahaara Mind is used to clinging on to objects of senses. But when you give them some other objects to cling on, that’s what different guided meditations are for. That is called Pratyahara – means the substitute food for mind, a substitution for mind to come inside. So you danced, it was a substitution, see how wonderful it was, so this is called Pratyahara – a 92 substitute food for mind to dive inside. tatahaparmavashitesriaanaam that brings all our senses, our body, everything together as one whole, you feel I am one whole, you feel you are one whole. [PDF p.92]

sutra.meaning: These three together are called Samyama

sections.insight: Integration leads to mastery. The three flow seamlessly from one to the other.
sections.gurudevInsight: Same is the case with the human consciousness, human mind. Either the seed can be dormant for years together, keeping its possibility within itself or start blossoming, start sprouting; the spouting of the seed of human consciousness is viveka, Discrimination, wisdom. Freedom comes with viveka or discrimination. All other species in this creation are governed by nature, totally, they don’t need discrimination nor do they have freedom. Human consciousness, human mind have this possibility of freedom, has been given freedom so it is also given discrimination. [PDF p.80]
